ops.title: The Swift widget can break against a fusekit bump with every Go gate green
ops.body:
`widget-test` is the only job that compiles `widget/`, and it needs macOS plus
Xcode, so nothing local or in the Go gates catches a Swift API break. The
dk-v021-migration branch carried one from the fusekit v1.15.x -> v1.16.0
migration all the way to the ship: `CatalogBroker.Configuration.init` dropped
`expectedRuntimeBuild` and `noProgressTimeout` in fusekit 24ae0d7, and cc-pool's
widget kept passing them. Build, vet, golangci-lint, the full -race suite,
suite-pins, wirebuildgen -check, and both release scripts were all green; the
break surfaced only on the first push, as `error: extra arguments at positions
#3, #4 in call`.

Reproduce and verify the widget locally with the exact commands ci.yml runs,
from `widget/`:
  xcodegen generate
  xcodebuild -project CCPoolStatus.xcodeproj -scheme CCPoolStatus \
    -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath build build test \
    CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-"
Run those before pushing any fusekit or daemonkit bump.

Two facts worth keeping, both initially guessed wrong and settled by reading
source:
- Dropping `expectedRuntimeBuild` loses nothing. v0.20.9 checked the build
  client-side after connecting (SocketClientAPI.swift:101). v0.21 rejects it
  server-side inside the mandatory handshake — internal/wire/server.go:268
  refuses a business lane whose schema the daemon does not accept, with
  ResponseCodeBuildMismatch. The client presents
  FuseKitTransportProtocol.wireBuild, a content digest, so a mismatched
  extension is refused before it dispatches a call.
- FUSEKIT_BUILD_ID is still set in production, by fusekit's own
  holder/plan.go:443, which builds the LaunchAgent that
  internal/statusapp/deployment.go:271 installs. cc-pool sets no Env of its own,
  which makes it look absent from cc-pool alone. The widget's guard was dead
  because its output had no consumer, not because the variable was missing.
